article_meta_data.title: Physical activity and the risk of heart failure: a systematic review and meta-analysis

all_paragraphs.paragraph: Seven prospective studies were included in the high versus low analysis of total physical activity and heart failure risk, which included 12,496 cases and 329,768 participants. The summary RR for high versus low physical activity was 0.77 (95% CI 0.70–0.85, I2=48.7%, pheterogeneity=0.07).

Two prospective studies were included in the analysis of vigorous physical activity and risk of heart failure (3632 cases, 158,397 participants). The summary RR for high versus low vigorous physical activity was 0.66 (95% CI 0.59–0.74, I2=0%, pheterogeneity=0.63) and per 20 MET-hours/week was 0.64 (95% CI 0.52–0.79, I2=14.9%, pheterogeneity=0.28).

Sixteen prospective studies were included in the analysis of leisure-time physical activity and risk of heart failure (>73,391 cases and 1,895,300 participants). The summary RR for high versus low leisure-time activity was 0.74 (95% CI 0.68–0.81, I2=88.0%, pheterogeneity<0.0001).
Four prospective studies were included in the dose–response analysis. The summary RR was 0.89 (95% CI 0.83–0.95, I2=66.8%, pheterogeneity=0.03, n=4) per 20 MET-hours per day of total activity.
